title: A Rick in King Mortur's Mort (plot)
text:
When Morty's offered a gift from a stranger, Rick tells him not to accept. Does Morty listen? No, he does not, and he's sucked into a messy adventure.

Morty drags Rick to a galactic pop-up restaurant located on an asteroid, to Rick's displeasure. While waiting in line, Morty picks up the dropped sandwich of two armored knights and tries to return it to them, politely declining their offer for him to keep the sandwich since he prefers to stand in line. One of the knights, Sir Helios, offers Morty his sword and his title as a Knight of the Sun. Rick discourages Morty from taking it, but Morty gets pressured by the knights and various other aliens offering to take it instead to go ahead and take the sword. Sir Helios dubs Morty "Sir Mortaniel" and kills himself with the sword. Rick watches in bewilderment as Morty is abruptly transported with the other knight to the Sun, then questions why the other aliens are not simply eating the dropped food. One of the patrons reveals they are paid by the pop-up to stand there to drive up business, which Rick suspected.

Morty arrives on the Sun to find it contains a medieval-like feudalist society living on a massive walkway, and agrees at the encouragement of the other knights and the King of the Sun to join them as an immortal being. That is, until he learns that a requirement of new knights is to cut off their penis. He promptly declares he is no longer interested, to the Knights' shock. Rick arrives to help Morty get out of his situation, but the King of the Sun demands Morty best him in combat if he wishes to leave. Rick gives Morty an AI Sword, which allows Morty to defeat the King easily. However, this backfires when the King relinquishes his crown and the Solar Scepter, declaring Morty is now King of the Sun before also killing himself. The Knights hail "King Mortaniel" but Rick and Morty promptly leave through a portal.

Back in the garage, Morty expects Rick to rub his recent debacle in his face. To his surprise, Rick decides not to, claiming Morty ignoring him at the pop-up made him realize how low he let Morty's opinion of him get. He agrees to be 22% nicer to Morty for at least one adventure. Their moment is interrupted by the arrival of the Knights of the Sun, whose duty is to follow him all day. They continue to trail Morty even to the Smith Family breakfast. The Knights explain that they and the King are meant to protect the Solar Scepter, which all planets in the solar system orbit, which is why they keep it on the Sun. Morty promptly reveals this is not true by explaining the basic physics of the solar system to the knights and revealing he has had the scepter on Earth. The Knights, angered that they cut off their penises for nothing, march off in a huff. At first, it seems that Morty has successfully used science and logic to destroy a religion, which the whole family praises him for. However, their celebration is interrupted by the sky changing color and all their electricity malfunctioning. One of the Knights, who missed everything because he went to the bathroom, explains the Sons of the Moon are attacking the Sun, but should be held off by a series of interplanetary treaties so long as the Knights stay together. He awkwardly backs out of the house upon realizing what happened.

Rick and Morty arrive at a neutral zone to find all the representatives from the various planets' rulers arguing over the sudden disappearance of the Knights of the Sun. Morty tries to interrupt through his authority as King of the Sun, but a magic hag reveals to the council that the Knights have disbanded. Lithdor, one of the Viscounts of Venus, questions Morty's legitimacy. Morty tries to prove it by revealing the Scepter, only to rather quickly learn that the Knights' claim that all planets orbit around it was symbolic: the Scepter actually denotes who rules the solar system, and all the rulers of the planets promptly start fighting for it while Rick and Morty make their escape.

A bloody solar war breaks out across the solar system as Rick uses his technology to protect Earth. Morty suggests they try jumping universes again, but Rick proposes they actually commit to this universe and try something else. Morty finally explodes, accusing Rick of pulling another "Vat of Acid" to rub Morty being wrong in his face again. Rick reiterates that he is just trying to do better, leading Morty to suspect he is a robot or a clone. Rick brushes off this accusation, and encourages Morty to think of something. Morty tracks down the Knights of the Sun to try to get them to return to the Sun. The Knights, who have become addicted to heroin in their despair over their loss of purpose, refuse to return to the Sun. Morty offers to cut his penis off if they do, which they point out would be pointless as he no longer needs to do it as king: Morty promises to do it anyway, which convinces them. Privately, of course, Morty is distraught, so Rick pulls him aside and promises to help him not have to actually cut it off using multiple fail-safes.

The Knights of the Sun reunite, prompting most of the planets to declare an end to the war. However, Lithdor suspects trickery and comes to the walkway to oversee the "Stumping of the King's Stem." First, he has Morty step through a machine that scans for "nanotechnological hologram dicks". Rick accounted for this, and Morty steps through with ease. But Lithdor then has Morty step through a second machine that checks for "emergency clone dicks." Morty quickly throws his away before stepping through the machine and passes once again. The third test, the old hag from before, reveals the presence of a "prosthetic/witchcraft dick", which he once again throws away. With all alternatives exhausted, Rick and Morty promptly make a run for it. During their escape, Rick applauds Morty for standing his ground and trying to solve the problem himself. However, stuck on a ledge above the surface of the Sun, they realize they need to pull their last option, which Rick is reluctant to do but Morty accepts is their only chance, and they promptly leap into the surface of the Sun.

One of the Knights is shown telling the story of "King Morty the Molten" and Rick's death from leaping into the Sun to some pages, telling of how their bones floated to the top and they even checked they died in the real Sun, not a vat of fake Sun. This prompted the knights to finally do away with their "stem stumping." It is revealed Rick and Morty snuck back to the walkway to learn what happened while they were gone, despite Morty pointing out they are risking ruining their whole escape by coming back. One of the pages walks by and realizes Morty is alive, but is easily convinced not to tell anyone when Morty points out the only thing that will come of revealing his survival is the page having to cut off his penis.

In the post credit scene, Special Agent Mongo Bongo arrests the Hot Dog Vendor at the Restaurant Asteroid for illegal hot dog trafficking. After finding more hot dogs in another area, he releases the hot dogs at the beach before he himself is captured by a bird.

title: A Ricker Runs Through It (plot)
text:
Forgotten passwords, humanoid authenticator robots, IT Cloud people and computer hacking hogs equals a smart house attacking Rick and Co. Just another day in the Smith family residence.

Rick drunkenly locks himself out of his garage security system, arguing with Morty about it. Their argument is interrupted by a call from Reese, a friend of Rick and Morty’s who invites the pair on a fishing trip, which Morty is excited about. After returning home from the trip, it is revealed that Reese is a robot that Rick uses to unlock his security system when he gets locked out. Morty is furious about this revelation and tries to prevent Rick from terminating him by taking the robot to a dimension filled with hog people who work to keep Rick’s flask filled with liquor. Meanwhile, Rick calls a tech support company who transfers the consciousness of one of their technicians into Jerry’s body. The hog people end up using Reese to take over control of Rick’s tech in the house, leading to the family fighting against their own household appliances and furniture. After receiving help from the technician in Jerry’s body, they shut off the hog people’s control of the tech, but the hog people send a brainwashed Reese to attack the family. Reese is only subdued after regaining his consciousness in response to Rick and Morty arguing with each other. The situation is fully resolved by Rick allowing the technician to transfer its consciousness into Reese. After it leaves, Rick begins drinking heavily again, disappointing Morty.

In the post credits scene, Rick is locked out of his garage system again and a man shows up saying he is a new neighbor wanting to hang out, so Morty stabs him thinking he is another robot. Right after stabbing the neighbor, Rick gets a call from Georgie Boy, who shows up to the garage as the new Reese, much to Morty’s dismay.

title: Erickerhead (plot)
text:
Thanks to a portal mishap, Rick’s head gets cut off from his body forcing Morty and Summer to get him fixed before things get out of hand. Then again, when has anything gone right for this family?

At a fast-food restaurant on some distant planet, Morty and Summer were waiting for Rick to finish his meal. Rick was eating like he was starving. Morty reminded Rick to hurry up, because he had promised to take them to an amazing place. Rick said that amazing place was here: unlimited fast food and bottomless alien beer in a giant beer garden. This was the pinnacle of consciousness, what the religious people call the breast of god.

After Rick finished his meal, they helped Rick leave. Morty suddenly realized they had driven here earlier and Rick seemed to have given the car keys to this leopard. Rick then opened a spatial portal, and Summer, seeing this, stopped him from entering. She told Morty to find the keys quickly.

Rick had dragged Summer through a teleportation gate to a street selling human body parts. And to top it all off, he even poked his head out to talk to Morty about some theoretical nonsense. The gate then closed, severing the upper and lower parts of Rick's head. Both Morty and Summer, witnessing the whole scene, were utterly terrified.

Summer approached the lower part of her grandfather's body and saw that the Portal Gun had also been severed by the gate. Rick's head, however, had sprouted an airbag system allowing him to breathe without lungs. Rick's AI system reported detecting an external intrusion. Summer swore she hadn't actually touched it.

Hearing the AI ​​say it was preparing to activate the self-destruct mechanism of the seven nuclear devices in his body, Summer was terrified. She tried calling Rick, but to no avail. So Summer had to call Morty instead. Morty swore it wasn't his fault, but Summer just wanted to ask how to turn off the self-destruct mechanism.

Rick told Summer to flip the body over. After fumbling around for a while, Summer managed to turn off Rick's self-destruct mechanism. Hearing Summer's sigh of relief, Rick gently reminded her not to relax. He said the body was in the wrong place. It was a criminal's hideout. The police wouldn't be able to do anything about it.

Summer wondered how Rick's head was still alive and could speak so clearly. But anyway, she had found the key. It was in Rick's blue shirt. Summer said the Portal Gun was useless. She thought everyone was in serious trouble. Rick said they were on the same planet. Theoretically, they should be fine.

Rick told Summer to go to a alien shopkeeper's place and stay there. Rick then sent Summer the address. He felt that being beheaded like this was truly exhilarating. Summer, seeing how long the journey was, was a little discouraged. She tried to experiment to see if this body had any mode that could help. Unexpectedly, the rocket on Rick's leg launched, attracting the covetous gazes of everyone around.

Seeing this, Summer quickly helped the headless body away. Crazy Randy and Randall, seeing Rick's attractive physique, followed them. The people here treated Rick's lower body as a gift from heaven. Everyone wanted to touch it. Summer, of course, didn't want anyone touching her grandfather.

After punching one guy in the backside, she carried Rick's body into a nearby alley. Summer dropped a parachute to block the path of the guys in front of her. The old man continued firing missiles from Rick's feet to shake off the pursuing crowd. Seeing the tech-savvy guys getting closer and closer, Summer transformed Rick's headless body into a scooter to escape from that chaotic place.

The scene shifts to a hospital, where Morty is wiping drool from his grandfather's head when a doctor walks in. He asks Morty if he understands what he just signed. Did he really agree to do that? Morty wonders what's going on. The doctor replies that Morty has signed a decapitation surgery consent form. Morty is shocked to hear the doctor say that his grandfather's upper body is meant to replace his head.

The doctor reassures Morty, telling him not to worry, that he's already called the police. Morty, though somewhat resentful of Rick, doesn't want to make a big deal out of it. Rick praises Morty for being utterly useless. As Rick told his grandson to look at that nosy, meddling fool. He bet that guy had already called security. Rick panicked and told Morty to run. Morty quickly grabbed Rick's head and dashed out of there as fast as he could. He hailed a taxi, threw Rick's head inside, and told the driver to go. Morty called Rick the worst grandfather in the world. Rick said he wasn't Morty's grandfather, just his head. Morty wondered if there was any difference.

Rick said he used to think that way too, but after waiting for an hour, there was still no sign of anything. Rick had a strange feeling. Although his mind was clearer, his airbag was almost empty. Rick reminded Morty that they needed to upgrade him immediately, otherwise he would ascend to heaven, and then the two of them would be in big trouble. Just then, a news report appeared on the TV stating that a severed head was trying to kidnap a child.

The authorities were on high alert and, to be clear, there would be a generous reward. The taxi driver's eyes lit up at the sight of the gold mine in the car. Morty, however, struck first. He used Rick's head to knock the driver unconscious. Morty asked his grandfather where they were going. Rick was completely helpless. Because lying down, he couldn't see anything at all.

The scene shifts to Summer, who has dragged the lower part of her grandfather's body to her boss. Summer says that Rick asked her to stay there. He's been beheaded. The head seemed to still be alive. Summer didn't understand why she'd told the alien shopkeeper about it. The alien shopkeeper said it was fine.

He boasted that he and Rick were best friends, the kind who looked out for themselves. Summer asked the alien shopkeeper if he had a way to make this thing less useless. As soon as the alien shopkeeper touched it, the body started thrashing around. It crawled into a corner and sat there trembling. They tried to calm it down. But Summer realized it didn't have ears to hear. Seeing this, the alien shopkeeper attached some kind of device to Rick's lower body.

He said it would help detect infrared sound waves and everything ape-like creature like Summer needed. Summer then called Morty to tell Rick the news. The two of them were being relentlessly pursued by the cops. Morty said he was busy, and Rick needed an air filter and new weapons, otherwise Morty would kill him.

Summer told the two of them to hurry to the alien shopkeeper's place. It reeked of gasoline; she liked it at first, but the smell made her nauseous. Morty told Rick it was the electronics store, but they didn't have a penny left. Hearing this, Rick told his grandson to use his brain. And so, Morty crashed into a convenience store and dragged Rick's head out to blackmail them for a bunch of spare parts.

Rick said he was very proud of his grandson. The landlady immediately recognized it as the kidnapper's head. Rick loudly boasted that he had laser eyes, scaring the two women. He told them to bring out their computer chips. The scene shifts to Summer, who is sitting huddled with Rick's body, when the alien shopkeeper and the crazy Randy walk in.

Randy thought this was a real windfall. He thought Rick's body was quite appealing, not like a ZM training or anything. Summer was utterly speechless with this so-called best friend. She questioned the alien shopkeeper, asking if he'd betrayed them as soon as he left the room. The alien shopkeeper asked if she knew how much Rick Sanchez's body was worth. Summer then taken Rick to another mechanic: Rachel, she he was clearly prettier and smarter than the alien shopkeeper. After saying that, Summer snapped over the alien shopkeeper's stall to trip him and ran away. Randy ordered his gang to quickly capture the guy. As Summer stepped out the door, several of Randy's henchmen, who had been waiting there since the afternoon, were already there. She was about to make her move when the body acted first. It blocked one guy's punch and gently severed the head of the one standing behind.

Summer was completely blown away by the sight. The two of them then quickly boarded a subway train. They hadn't even settled into their seats when Randy's gang arrived to cause trouble again. The man ordered others to finish off Summer and Rick's body. Both sides charged at each other, their weapons clashing. The twos worked together and thoroughly defeated Randy's gang.

Seeing how useless the henchemen were, Randy ordered his accomplice to shoot from behind. Rick shielded Summer with his body, being blown out the window. Luckily, he managed to grab onto Summer's stick. He then pulled them all onto the roof of the ship to continue the fight.

After the ship stopped, the twos had finished dealing with Randy's gang. Seeing this, Randy ordered his two companions to join him. They asked Randy if he just saw what Summer and Rick's body just did to their comrades before cursed Randy, calling him a terrible leader. Then they left. Randy was forced to intervene. He tried to attack Rick's body but Summer stopped him.

Summer even saw Rick's body use a chokehold. Randy thought he was going to die. But no, Rick's body hugged him. Randy had a strange feeling. He didn't know what to say anymore. Summer watched Randy walk away. She wondered if hugging someone really made them less aggressive. Rick's body then hugged Summer which a similar feeling. On Rick's side, there both Rick and Morty The were surrounded by a swarm of police. Rick was busily eating various components when Summer called. Summer said the alien shopkeeper had betrayed them and she needed a new meeting point. Rick replied that they would meet at the spaceport if Rick survived this.

Just then, a police call interrupted Summer's call. They said they might sacrifice hostages. The store couple were terrified. The cops, of course, were now unleashing their democratic side. Rick cursed them, calling them a bunch of bastards. He told Morty that he had upgraded enough. Now, they should lift his head.

Rick then fired a laser at the cops. Surprisingly, no ones were sacrificed. They only lost a few limbs. Morty thought this less violence was good. Who knows, maybe their TV show would become more humane. At this point, a group of armed soldiers broke through the ceiling and climbed down. Rick snapped all the cables, causing them to fall and twist their backs.

Rick then ordered Morty to go collect more parts. He would then hack into the system via a makeshift computer. The cops suddenly received a call from headquarters, saying they were wrong about their target. The colonel sighed, saying this is the worst scandal in the industry, and ordered the entire team to retreat. Rick said he had reduced the level of violence.

He asked Morty if he liked it. Morty, of course, liked it very much. He then rushed Rick and a pile of parts to the airport. The scene shifts to a first-class cabin, where Rick is watching tennis and crying his eyes out. Just as Morty finishes wiping Grandpa's tears, a flight attendant with four breasts approaches. Morty thinks this is just too much. The scene shifts to Summer, whose body and neck are already at the airport waiting for Morty and Rick

Before parting ways, Rick's body confided in a handwritten note, saying how much he loved the children and encouraging Summer to believe in herself, because both Beth and Jerry were fools. Summer was very grateful for that. She didn't expect the neck to be so warm. Morty then approached, carrying Rick's head, both feeling quite sad about having to separate. One might expect the reunion scene to be touching, but it was incredibly cold.

As soon as they met, they started fighting, neither wanting to be bound by the other's other half. Seeing the two halves of Rick wreaking havoc, Summer guessed that each part was too happy to be alone, and they wanted to eliminate each other to avoid being reunited.

The scene shifts to Morty and Summer sitting on the Space Cruiser, arguing about how Summer, after spending several hours with her old self, suddenly wanted to eliminate her newly acquired brain. Summer is annoyed with her brother for siding with the head. Just then, Rick calls. He reassures Morty that everything is fine. He's on his way to a metallurgical facility to find a new master.

Rick thinks there's no need for him and his body to fight; they should just go their separate ways. Summer is horrified that Rick isn't himself anymore. Her grandfather, hearing her voice, immediately recognizes that she's sided with his body Summer thinks this is a disaster. If Beth finds out they've lost Rick, they'll be in big trouble.

Rick, on the other hand, would be furious if he knew he was going to die this way. The scene shifts to Rick arriving at the metallurgical facility and seeing Rachel walking out. When Rachel saw Rick's head, she was shocked. Rick was busy talking about how he needed a new body when his body approached. Rick lost his composure.

He asked if the body and Rachel had done anything. He thought that if he confessed, he would ruin their friendship. His body said they had a classic ten-year relationship that was more than friendship but less than love. Rachel admitted it had ruined everything, but she was ecstatic. Hearing this, Rick became furious.

He told the fleeing body that the disgusting friend-destroyer with the huge penis would pay for it. Rachel try to prevent to wreak havoc on her house, but it was too late. Rick had already blown everything away and run outside to settle the score with the his body. Morty then called Rachel, who said the both Rick and Rick's body were there. By the way, she reminded him to delete her number.

Before the two parts of Rick actually started punching each other, the upper part preemptively attacked with psychological tactics. He scolded the lower part, calling him a womanizer who ruined his life. He always messed things up, got drunk and damaged relationships, and even secretly ate sweets at night. From now on, the first part of Rick swore he would break free from the lower part forever.

The body also tried to say something, but Rick didn't understand, and then the two of them clashed. The first part of Rick was trying to use his tongue to remove the sensor attached to the body's neck, but that was utterly useless. And to make matters worse, the Rick's head's body was cut in half. Rick's head then unleashed a terrifying sonic wave. Unfortunately, the body had no ears, so this attack was completely ineffective. The body then lunged towards Rick.

He panicked and quickly rolled down onto the control panel below. Rick's head then manipulated the robotic arms to clash with Rick's body. Both of them wreaked havoc, creating a spectacular scene. Morty and Summer arrived just in time to witness this epic battle. Rick's head, having managed to push the body back a little, felt triumphant.

Seeing this, the body immediately activated its emergency mode. Rick's head was now truly overwhelmed. The body removed all of the robotic arms from the alchemy area and destroyed the control panel where Rick's head was standing. The body then grabbed the head, and the body was about to dip Rick's severed head into a hot pot right there. Summer was horrified at the sight.

Both of them tried to stop the two parts of their grandfather. Rick's head, terrified, came up with an idea. The two parts of the body made some kind of agreement and dragged each other into a control room nearby. After a long period of reconciliation, the complete Rick awkwardly emerged. Summer immediately realized that Rick had been performing oral sex in there. Morty felt this was truly horrifying and disgusting.

Rick denied it, but it was insignificant. Summer stopped teasing her grandfather. She told everyone to leave, because the oil refinery was about to collapse. The scene shifts to the three of them driving the Space Cruiser home. Rick said it was a really chaotic Tuesday. Summer just hoped her grandfather would learn to be kinder to himself.

Rick also thought that from tomorrow he would have to live a healthier life. Of course, the two grandchildren didn't believe it at all. So the next morning, he woke Morty and Summer up early for exercise. Afterward, they won a bronze medal in a swimming competition on some distant planet. Morty and Summer couldn't understand why they were getting involved in this kind of thing. To make matters worse, he couldn't even remember the name of the female Olympic athlete next to him.

In the post credits scene, Rick is about to leave through a portal for another task. Morty worries he might decapitate himself again only to reveal he was messing with him. He does an impression of Porky Pig complete with a random tune since Warner Bros won’t let them use the Looney Tunes ending melody.

title: Field of Dreams (plot)
text:
Thanks to some interdimentional traveling, Morty ends up traveling to different universes where he finds variants of him who have died and his family trying to move on leading Morty to have an existential crisis and gain more connections.

Rick and Morty are lying on the ground, about to die from having their legs detached from their torso. They and the rest of the family ate chili that was too spicy, resulting in everyone's violent deaths. Shortly after checking out, a Rick from another dimension hosts an estate sale, and is followed by various other versions of Rick, including our Rick and Morty. They can buy anything they want to take for themselves, as the family is dead, but Morty doesn't particularly enjoy looting a dead version of his family. He meets Sunglasses Morty, who is not interested in the estate sale. Instead, he visits funerals of their dead family in other dimensions to hear their heartfelt eulogies. He goes by himself with his own portal gun called the Portal Gun Jr.. Sunglasses Morty shows Morty Smith the dead Morty's version of the Portal Gun Jr. stashed in a box before leaving.

Morty asks to visit his own funeral. Rick is mostly preoccupied by the friction-free rotational platform he got at the estate sale, but doesn't forbid him to go. In a dimension where everyone has big legs and tiny torsos, he sees his dead self and learns that he got microwaved to death by his Rick. He is about to leave, but sees Big Leg Jessica kiss the corpse and decides to keep visiting more funerals. He witnesses a lot of dead Morties, sad families, and strange things happening to his corpse.

At one of his funerals, he finds a Morty that happens to be smarter, more athletic, and loved by many people, especially his Jerry. Even his dog is a large Bernese Mountaindog rather than whatever tiny Snuffles was. He is caught spying by their dog and taken back home by the surprised family. He tells them that he's from another dimension, and was able to visit thanks to the work of Rick. They tell him that their version of Rick was cast out for being too drunk and destructive. Morty stays with them briefly and gets comfortable but decides to leave his "Good" family, worried that his family is worried about him. Moral Jerry allows him to return whenever he wants, as they still mourn their Morty. Morty portals back to find his family unbothered by his absence.

Morty later decides to portal back to the Mort's family. They go eat at a teppanyaki place, and Morty tells them stories of his adventures with Rick, although they are disturbed that Rick allows him to repeatedly die. Morty begins to bond with Good Jerry, finding him a better father than his Jerry. They go to Good Jerry's cabin in the woods and have fun together. Good Jerry also tells Morty about his Morty (nicknamed Mort), who died in a rock-climbing accident, and lets out tears. Morty comforts him and asks to be the son he no longer has, but Moral Jerry wants him to break the Portal Jr so he can never return home. They struggle over the Portal Jr, which gets dropped and destroyed. Good Jerry turns out to be a little crazy, as he is obsessed with making his son stronger.

Morty runs away and discovers Mort's former belongings. He learns that Good Jerry caused Mort to fall to his death by forcing him to free solo El Capitan. Morty takes Mort's shoes and evades Good Jerry, who is hunting him. He takes a bus ride all the way to MIT, where he finds Sober Rick as a professor, and asks for help in crafting a portal gun. Before they go back to his home to work on it, Rick makes a speech at an Alcoholics Anonymous meeting, sharing his life experience of losing his Diane, drifting away from Beth, and staying sober for 17 years. Despite the loss of his family, Sober Rick is happy, thanks to his relationship with Uli, his new wife. Meanwhile, Good Jerry tracks Morty to Boston, and later finds Sober Rick's address.

Sober Rick works on the portal gun, but fails to create a working portal repeatedly. He accidentally lashes out at Uli, and worries that she will leave him like Diane did. Morty tells him that Diane was erased from infinity by the Omega Device and that he did nothing wrong. Morty continues to goad Sober Rick into creating the portal gun, which begins to drive him mad in his pursuit of the multiverse. He relapses on drinking and starts to resemble the Rick that Morty is familiar with. Uli leaves him, and Morty admits that he kinda ruined Sober Rick's life.

Eventually, they are able to create a working portal. Before Morty can go through, they are stopped by the Mort's family, who holds them at gunpoint. Sober Rick throws his cat through, revealing that the portal is still flawed when it returns as flesh. Sober Rick and the Mort's family get into a fight, and Good Jerry accidentally shoots the portal. The portal goes haywire, sucking parts of the garage inside. In the chaos, Sober Rick is shot by Good Jerry, Sober Rick shoots Good Jerry with a failed portal gun that dehydrates him, Good Summer is bisected by the portal exploding, and Good Beth commits suicide. Morty despairs, mourning the loss of the Mort's family, Sober Rick, and being unable to return home.

Suddenly, the Estate Salesman Rick arrives and announces an estate sale, as all of the Mort's Dimension's family is dead. Rick is there and takes Morty home, but not before Morty turns Sunglasses Morty into a dog with a long neck for saying he "looks like shit". Sunglasses Rick then uses the same long-neck dog gun on himself.

Morty is traumatized, but the family has no idea what happened and continue their normal routines. Morty attempts to sleep, but is dragged out by a drunk Rick. Rick fixed an issue that Morty had with the rotational platform that he seemingly ignored earlier. They go on a motorcycle ride into the sunrise, where Rick allows Morty to drive from the backseat. Rick is proud of guiding him and calls himself Morty's dad. Morty agrees, and is ultimately content with his adventures with Rick.

In the post credits scene in an unknown spacecraft, Mr. Poopybutthole reflects on how Season 9 went, all the while being used as a test subject for Amy in an attempt to locate the variant of her husband that he replaced. However, the experiment unexpectedly malfunctions, and the pod containing Mr. Poopybutthole, Amy, and other scientists suddenly disappears.

title: Mortgully: The Last Rickforest (plot)
text:
Rick and Morty’s adventure to collect special sap from an ancient tree hits a snag when the titular tree captures them in an endless system of evolution and life. Fortunately, the two have their own ways of beating the system.

Rick and Morty land on a rainforest-like alien planet in order to harvest a certain sap from a particular tree. The tree in question that they attempt to cut down is revealed to be alive. The tree is disgusted at Rick and Mortys' destruction of nature for selfish purposes. They are grabbed by its tentacle-like roots and dragged into the ground, where they magically turn into balls of energy and are thrown into a hollow earth.

They are reincarnated as single-celled amoebas from their life energies. A fellow amoeba tells them they're not the only ones that tried to raid the planet, as they are surrounded by other "cellmates". The cellmates are unable to return to their regular bodies, hence everyone is trapped as though they were in a prison. The amoeba then kills and eats both of them, who immediately reincarnate back. They do the same to him, and decide that the only way out is to evolve into a stronger form.

Rick and Morty start by using mitosis to evolve into fish. They grow lungs and begin to walk on land, and decide that their goal is to escape the cycle of reincarnation by reaching the surface. To do so, they need to reach the giant root of the Tree Warden in the center of the hollow earth. However, Morty chokes on air after seeing the horrors of the cycle of life and suffocates to death, forcing Rick to drown himself to meet back with him.

They try using other animals to reach the tree. They evolve into spiders, but get stuck in their own webbing and die. They evolve into birds and are able to reach the base of the tree, but can't do anything else. They also discover that the tree itself is aggressive when it squeezes both of them to death. They eventually evolve into monkeys in order to gain hands. The two of them assert dominance by invading a water hole inhabited by apes, many of whom are killed by Rick with a spear he crafted. In the chaos, Morty is crushed by a dead ape, while Rick chooses to stay a monkey to find a way for them both of to escape.

Morty meets another, less aggressive cellmate who also dislikes the cycle of violence. He has chosen to become part of the life cycle instead of killing to attempt to escape in the hopes that the warden will notice and set him free. Morty joins him and a few others, starting as a bee. It is short-lived, as they are all killed by a gorilla who destroy their hive to eat honey.

Meanwhile, Rick has captured a bunch of animals/cellmates to use as slaves, ruling them like a dictator. He soon decides to climb the tree, though due to the tree being dangerous he hands the work over to his slaves and observes the tree instead to track its traps. His most loyal slave, Gorilla 3, dies to poison gas after making some progress. Others do not make it much further, racking up many bodies. Rick also tries other ways to destroy the tree, such as a giant saw and molten lava, but they are also repelled.

Morty ends up shitting and eating a lot of shit as various other animals. He gets disillusioned of being a peaceful shit-eating animal, having made no progress to escape the hollow earth. While airing his worries to the leader of the group, he becomes inspired to take a different approach. He returns to an amoeba, but instead decides to become a plant instead. He starts as phytoplankton and gets dragged around by the ocean until he reaches land. He turns into moss, then a small plant, then an apple tree, which then has its apples eaten and seeds spread around, creating more apple trees. Morty continues this cycle until his swathes of trees reaches the base of the tree, now surrounded by significantly more bodies over the course of Rick's efforts. He becomes a beanstalk to climb the tree, which does not attempt to stop him as a fellow plant, and breaks through the surface. There, the Tree Warden kills him, revealing that he was never meant to escape due to the cycle of death being its food source.

Rick, having watched Morty climb the tree, commits suicide to rendezvous with Morty. With both of them now knowing the true nature of the tree, they devise a plan to defeat the tree. Rick seals himself and the other cellmates into a cave, while Morty provides them all sustenance as a massive all-encompassing plant within. They live peaceful, content lives, and two of them even marry.

Due to nobody dying, the hollow earth and the Tree Warden dry up, as both were being sustained on death. The Tree Warden uproots itself to go investigate and finds the cave as the only thing covered in plants. The plants, who are all Morty, move to uncover Rick and the cellmates, who ambush the Tree Warden. They pull him out by using harpoons and vines from multiple directions. The Tree Warden dies, and everyone celebrates. With the cycle of reincarnation gone, and nobody having magically returned to their original bodies automatically, Rick and Morty avoid the potential awkwardness by telling everyone to close their eyes and believe really hard. They then fly away in a hot air balloon and off the planet in the Space Cruiser.

They return home, having only been gone for about a day despite the extensive time spent evolving due to the planet's proximity with a black hole. They walk in on Summer doing biology homework, but when Morty attempts to help her, he discovers that he learned nothing from the whole ordeal.

In the post credit scene, Rick and Morty grab lunch at an alien burger restaurant when they walk by an alien who they vaguely recognize as Hyena #3, one of the animals they’ve seen in the Hollow Earth system, and he gives them a look. The two realize the animals have returned to normal and have escaped the planet but try not to make their identities known while also mentioning that they looked way different than they thought. After they leave Hyena #3 sits with his husband (also returned to normal) and tells him about his encounter with Rick and Morty but his husband already knows and Hyena #3 gets upset at him for stealing his story.

title: Nomortland (plot)
text:
Jerry befriends another Jerry from another dimension, only for him to take him to another dimension.

In the morning, a Five O' Clock shadow bearded Jerry is seen calmly eating cereal at the dinner table while the other members of the family walk past into the kitchen. Space Beth and Rick discuss something while Summer is looking for her Kombucha, which Morty threw away, in the fridge. Beth asks Jerry if he has seen the car keys. The Jerry at the dinner table freezes in silence before Beth mentions she has found the keys and leaves the house. Suddenly its revealed the Jerry at the dinner table is not our Jerry. Our Jerry was on the toilet and just got off it. Both Jerrys are surprised to see each other. The cereal eating Five O' Clock shadow bearded Jerry starts running out the house with our Jerry giving chase. our Jerry catches the mysterious Jerry. Asking him if he is a clone. It seems this mysterious Jerry is only interested in eating breakfast or lunch and has no ulterior mischievous motive.

Jerry and the mysterious version of him go to the mall to talk and eat. There he mentions that he is interested in taking a job at the retail store "American Eagle" in the mall. This causes our Jerry to be nicknamed "Eagleman" by the mysterious Jerry. After getting to eat his food, this mysterious Jerry drops the quote "the road provides" which our Jerry questions the meaning of. The mysterious Five O' Clock shadow bearded Jerry reveals he is a traveler from another dimension. They talk about their respective families. They return back to the house.

While this mysterious Jerry goes to Beth and Jerry's bedroom, our Jerry tries to distract Rick, who just pushed an ice block with an alien creature inside into the freezer, with an awkward small talk about the new "Naked and Alone" episode. the awkward small talk succeeds as Rick responses to Jerry's comment about the weird Naked and Alone contestant and his obsession with yak piss. the conversation ends with Jerry going to his bedroom and Rick being mad at him.

Jerry and the other Jerry visit varying dimensions through pathways without the use of a portal gun. They visit a dimension where everyone speaks in "Blah blah blah". They see a Rick and Morty angrily yelling at each other while pushing a giant ant into Rick's spaceship. our Jerry encounters this dimension's Summer and simple responds a "blah." to her blah blah cries.

During a montage, Jerry and the other Jerry visit a yarn dimension, a goat dimension and a hippie dimension.

By the end of the day, Mooch and Eagleman Jerry are sitting on the roof of their house in another dimension, sharing a beer as they talk about life. Time passes by, and Mooch and Eagleman start to make their way back to our Jerry’s dimension as promised, but they merely miss their connector, which is a portal that Rick and Morty shoot using a portal gun outside a taco store. The Jerrys panic, and Eagleman Jerry questions how he is going to get home then. Mooch reassures him, saying that this version of Rick and Morty shoots a portal there every week, but Eagleman continues to panic. As a last resort, Mooch reveals that they can travel through Grand Central to meet Boss Jerry, who is able to send them through an alternate line of portals back to the Parmesan dimension.

Unfortunately, their meeting with Boss Jerry ends up as a fluke as Eagleman insults him, resulting in him and Mooch being blacklisted from travelling before being sent back to Mooch’s original universe. It is then revealed that Mooch avoids his home because of his estranged relationship with his family and Beth remarrying. Upon learning this, Eagleman calls Mooch the “least cool Jerry” and forces him to confront his family. In the end, Jerry makes amends with his family and has his Rick portal him back to Grand Central.

As the two returned, they are pursued by Boss Jerry and his Jerry goons, chasing Mooch and Eagleman as they make their way back to the Parmesan dimension. The chase ends in a burlap sack portal, where Boss Jerry takes out a gun and attempts to kill them. As a last ditch effort, Mooch servers the line in the burlap sack, and the portal tears and collapses in on itself, seemingly killing Boss Jerry.

Mooch and Eagleman Jerry return to the Parmesan dimension, where they bid each other a fond farewell. Jerry's family angrily enters the room, causing Jerry to realize with surprise that they were worried about where he was. He pleasantly explains his absence as "me time", which the family is disgusted at. After they leave, Jerry flips over the coaster by the bed stand. Rick doubles back, and upon noticing the coaster and eyeing the closet, he knowingly remarks that this could be good for Jerry before leaving. Jerry quickly turns the coaster back right side up.

In the post credit scene, Beth walks into the dark living room to find a naked Rick watching TV and eating popcorn. It's revealed he is watching the new episode of "Naked and Alone". Next to him is a naked Jerry eating popcorn as well. Beth is disgusted by both, as they state it is the spirit of the show. As she walks away in disgust, Rick and Jerry make small talk about the nude guy in the "Naked and Alone" episode, as they did before in the episode.

title: Rick Fu Hustle (plot)
text:
A fender bender at Trader Joe’s leads to Rick and Morty making enemies out of a Kung Fu master with deadly hand techniques. Meanwhile Jerry has problems with his pool cleaner robot which soon takes on a life of its own.

The episode begins with Jerry and Beth arguing about how dirty the pool has become thanks to a cheap pool cleaner Jerry bought from guy behind the pool store not functioning properly. Beth asks why Jerry can't just call Keith the Pool Guy, but while he claims Keith was busy, it's more that he's insecure about Keith's looks. When Rick sees the pool, he offers to clean it himself, but Jerry refuses Rick's help. So, Rick lets Jerry figure this out on his own as he and Morty are finally going to Boob World.

Rick and Morty make a stop at Trader Joe's before going to Boob World, but they accidentally hit the back of someone's car. Rick starts an argument with the guy when he refuses to exchange information, irritating Morty as it's taking time away from Boob World, but the guy reveals himself to be a master martial artist and hits Rick with several pokes to his chest. The guy explains that he hit Rick with the five-step exploding heart technique, warning the latter that his heart will explode if he takes five steps forward.

In the Post Credit Scene, Beth is using her hair dryer to dry her hair which she has grown a sexual attachment to. Jerry catches her in the act to which Beth puts a Jerry mask on the dryer.

title: Ricks Days, Seven Nights (plot)
text:
Every year, Rick goes on vacation to another planet as his alternate persona Ted in order to relieve the stress of his life. This year, things are going to turn out very different.

On cold winter night, while driving, Ted was suddenly cut off by a deer. Ted's recreational vehicle braked sharply, losing control and skidding along the road.

Ted got out of the recreational vehicle, looked at the huge tear in the tire, turned on the radio, played some country music, and lit a flare to light it. He sawed off some branches to melt the rubber and used it to patch the punctured tire. After finishing the repairs, Ted packed up his tools.

He looked at the deer with great affection, not killing it. Ted then drove his old recreational vehicle to Dream Lanes, a local pub and bowling alley. Looking at the old photos and souvenirs, Ted and the people there seemed quite close. When Marjorie saw Ted, she was overjoyed. She knew she'd meet a handsome guy there.

The old friends felt the same way. As soon as they saw Ted, they swarmed around him like they were swarming around excrement. They all raised their glasses to celebrate Ted's return. The scene shifts to outside, where Little Mike asks Ted if he's still selling those PVC pipes. Why not try investing in HDPE? Ted replies that selling pipes alone was enough to keep him here. But he's sure no one wants to sell plastic. Besides, all the men just like stuffing pipes. After a few jokes, they all went home.

Meanwhile, Ted goes with Antonio to finish off the remaining beer. Ted asks Antonio if Marjorie is still opening late these days. Antonio replies that Marjorie's mother recently passed away, so she probably doesn't want to go home. Ted sighs. He says everyone has to run away from something. The scene shifts to a liquor store. The two are about to pay for their new beer when an armed Unnamed robber suddenly appears. He fired a warning shot and shouted, "Everyone, hand over your wallets!"

He was about to kill Ted when two robotic arms suddenly appeared from nowhere. One arm deflected the bullet, the other sent the Unnamed robber to his death. Ted stared intently at his palm. He felt utterly bewildered. Antonio was relieved that Ted was unharmed. The Country Store Liquor woman had already called the police.

Ted grabbed the beer and ran out, making a quick getaway. Despite Antonio and Country Store Liquor woman pleas for him to return, the scene shifts to Ted's recreational vehicle. He was examining himself in the mirror. After taking a sip of alcohol to muster courage, Ted took a kitchen knife from the drawer to test the elasticity of his skin.

Seeing Ted harming himself, the robotic arms appeared to stop him. They snatched the knife away and restrained him, silencing him. A holographic projection of Rick suddenly appeared and told Ted the whole story. The projected Rick said it seemed Ted had learned a few things about his body. In short, this gentleman named Ted wasn't a plastic pipe seller.

He was the smartest person who had ever existed, born 400 light-years ago. Ted was currently in Beloi 6E, a primitive place with great country music and snow-covered landscapes, much like Earth's home world in the early 1990s. Because he was fed up with living like the lord of all creatures in the 41-degree Celsius snow of Earth in the summer, Rick decided to erase all his memories except for his survival gear and come here to rest for two weeks before returning with a super-light head. After saying this, the projected Rick released Ted. He gave Test two choices. If something went wrong, he could press the red button, and Rick would return. If everything was fine,
press the blue button to erase this from his memory. And of course, Ted didn't choose either. Ted rushed out of the recreational vehicle, throwing up everything he'd just put in his mouth with a look of utter panic. Ted immediately went to Dream Lanes to call for help. Marjorie, seeing Ted's body was ice cold, helped him inside.

Ted sat drinking and confiding in Marjorie. Marjorie showed Test the disco ball she'd installed the last time Ted came. The two lay there, pouring out their hearts. And then they ended up sleeping together. After a sleepless night, Ted decided he had to make a deal with this.

Seeing Ted get out of bed, Marjorie begged him not to leave. Ted reassured Marjorie that he wouldn't leave. When Ted returned to the recreational vehicle one last time, Rick's holographic projection appeared again. He said he was there because Ted had ignored the previous instructions. Ted ignored Rick's incessant chatter. He set up the self-driving car. Then he jumped out.

Before the recreational vehicle crashed down into the ravine, Marjorie, watching, was speechless. The scene shifts to the old friends and Ted chatting at a fishing hole on a frozen lake. Ted says he'll stay here with everyone this year to watch the snow melt. Little Mike asks, "What about Ted's plastics company?" Ted shrugs.

He thinks it's not really exists. Hearing this, Ted's old friends thought he was drunk. They just sat there drinking and laughing. The scene shifts to nighttime, when everyone is fast asleep. Ted suddenly sees a strange light. It's coming from the egg-shaped spaceship in the pine forest nearby. Seeing this, he picks up his gun and approaches the spaceship to investigate.

At this point, Ted unexpectedly receives a call from Morty. The phone is hidden inside Ted's calf. Ted asks who's on the other end. Morty thinks to himself, "I'm in big trouble now." Anyway, he just needs his grandfather back inside the egg. Morty begs Ted not to pick a fight with Rick.

He just wants to get his grandfather home before something worse happens. Ted replies that nothing is worse than being another personality of Rick, just a suit for the old man to wear. Before Ted could finish his sentence, the spaceship forcibly took him back to Earth.

While Ted was in a life-or-death situation, his friends suddenly appeared, crashing into Rick's spaceship and rescuing him from certain defeat. Everyone asked if he was okay, what the hell was that thing, and if he was an alien or something. Ted said it was Rick's spaceship, and that no matter what, Ted wouldn't let Rick have his way.

The scene shifts to Dream Lanes, where Ted is begging Marjorie for help. Hearing this, Marjorie closes the shop early. The 90-year-old gamblers, hearing Marjorie's announcement, are displeased, as they've only played three rounds. Ted thanks Marjorie, making her promise not to return.

That very night, Marjorie made Ted promise not to lose his internet connection at her bowling alley. The scene shifts to Ted gritting his teeth in pain. He asks Big Mike to get rid of Rick's devilish technology. Bowser stuff explosives into a pile of bowling pins? Little Mike and Antonio will control the water spraying system. When everyone is ready, Ted orders Big Mike to cut it off. The scene shifts to Ted anxiously waiting.

He's strolling outside, waiting for Rick's technology to come and clash with him. The old men are already hiding behind bowling pins. Seeing the robots approaching, Ted orders them to act. The battlefield is chaotic; Bowser activate the explosive bowling balls, and simultaneously use the vending machine to fire bowling pins sending a number of robots to their demise

Seeing another swarm of robots rushing in, Ted activates the net system, capturing an entire oncoming group. At this point, Antonio's sprinkler system malfunctioned, and one robot was about to send Little Mike to his grave. Luckily, Ted jumped in to save the day. Ted then lured the robots to follow him. He was eliminating upon each one by one when he slipped and fell.

Fortunately, Marjorie returned, saving Tet from a devastating defeat. Marjorie activated the oil-spraying system, while Ted stood near, lighting the fire to send the drone robots to their graves. Everyone was celebrating their brief victory when they received devastating news: Marjorie had been impaled through the chest by a piece of metal. And so Marjorie passed away. He was carried in Ted's arms. Everyone give a minute of silence for Marjorie. Ted quickly wiped away his tears of grief.

He laid Marjorie's body down and pulled the corpse of a robot inside. Ted began to dissect it. At this moment, Ted's eyes suddenly transformed into magnifying glasses. He himself was frightened by the thing, but he quickly adapted to it. He continued his experiment, not forgetting to tell his old friends that he would find Rick first and kill him. Little Mike asked Ted if he needed any help. Ted replied that he needed everyone to leave, because he couldn't protect anyone.

Seeing the crisis, Antonio spoke up, saying that everyone here wouldn't let Marjorie die in vain. Big Mike agreed. That Rick might be a tough guy, but Ted had them, and wherever Ted went, they would follow. And so, Ted began using the robots' positioning to redraw the map.

Ted was delighted to know where Rick come from. They began dismantling everything, from Rick's recreational vehicle to Marjorie's bowling alley. All to build a spaceship based on Ted's design. Ted had also reprogrammed Rick's robotic arms, making them completely obedient to him.

After building a seemingly unscientific ship, they decided to let Ted and Big Mike pilot it. Antonio looked at a picture of himself with his wife, secretly hoping that this trip wouldn't be a pointless death. After the ship's doors were locked, Ted and Big Mike began to start it.

Looking outside, he saw himself and everyone else gradually ascending. Suddenly, a screw flew out, and everything started to fall apart, but at one point, the spaceship was unharmed. The group of people gradually flew out into space. They were stunned to see their magnificent home planet right before their eyes. Test said, "Now here come the best part."

He started the spaceship and sent it soaring through hyperspace, giving everyone a terrifying scare. With a loud crash, Ted's spaceship slammed into Smith Residence's garage. As Ted and his companions crawled out of the spaceship, another drunken projection of Rick appeared. If Ted could see this, then the previous projections were clearly useless. Ted ordered the old men to rush over and smash the videotape.

At that moment, a robot descended from the ceiling. It announced that it was forcibly shutting down the vacation mode. After saying that, it extended its arms to grab Ted and his friends. Ted tried to fight back, but it was utterly useless. To make matters worse, the robot ripped off all his robotic arms. While the two sides were fighting fiercely, Beth and her family went down to the garage.

She asked Ted, who still hasn't return to his original persona: Rick. What her father had done to ruin the garbage shredder. Seeing this, Big Mike immediately took Beth hostage. He ordered the Smith Family to turn it off, threatening to roast her alive. The Smith Family remained surprisingly calm. Beth couldn't understand why her father kept hanging out with these country bumpkins.

Ted asked Beth if she was Rick's daughter. Summer, hearing this, exclaimed that she couldn't believe she wasn't old enough to buy alcohol. She ordered the garage to retrieve the robot. As soon Bowser could speak, he told Big Mike to eliminate Beth. Ted quickly stopped his old friend. At this point, Morty ran down. He was relieved Rick was back but suddenly panicked when he realized the person in front of him was Rick, who was on vacation: Ted.

Jerry was too fed up to say anything; suddenly, having to pay for the extra garage repairment. Jerry, Beth and Summer returned to the pool to clear their minds. Ted recognized Morty's voice as the boy who had called him on the phone at his calf. Ted thought Morty was Rick's friend. Morty said something like that. More accurately, he was Rick's grandson. Bowser seeing their wrecked ship, thought everyone would have to stay there for a while. Morty hurried to find the red button.

Ted then asked his garage where Rick's tools were hidden. The garage was no longer polite; it showed Ted a bunch of technologies that Rick had created. At this point, Little Mike asked if Ted could lend him some of those stuff. The scene shifts to a bowling alley, where the old guys who had just stolen some of Rick's technology bring it out to Ted.

Ted still feeling bored. He went to order a few more pints of beer. The Unnamed Lux Ball employee asks Ted if he's part of that bunch of country bumpkins with robotic arms. Seeing Little Mike wrecking Unnamed Lux Ball employee's shop, the Unnamed Lux Ball employee immediately tells those old guys to leave. The scene shifts to Ted sitting dejectedly in the garage. At this point, the group of elderly people enter and say Beth is making pancakes.

Seeing Ted say he's busy, Little Mike offers to make him a laser eye. Ted coldly opens a spatial portal with Rick's Portal Gun and tells his old friends to go inside. Big Mike says he can see Marjorie's bowling alley over there and now everyone can go home.

Little Mike wonders if they won? So they took down that guy? Ted confirms that's right and tells everyone to go inside. Before leaving, Mike's group stole quite a bit of Rick's technology—you could say they took the whole garage. The following days were a series of miserable days for Ted. He spends his time soaking in the swimming pool. Both Beth and Space Beth were utterly terrified by what they saw.

Ted then went on a galactic drinking spree, fishing with some fish, getting high with a bunch of mushroom aliens, and wreaking havoc on a village of tiny people. Ted returned to his old pub, only to find it had become a supermarket: L-Mart. He went to the cemetery and saw three friends weeping over a small grave. Ted thought it was Marjorie, but no, it was Little Mike. The robotic arms had betrayed him.

Big Mike told Ted that he was the one who caused all this and that he was the fake alien. After saying this, Big Mike lunged at Ted, intending to fight him. Ted stopped time using Rick's technology and quickly made his escape, changing the scene. Ted was so helpless that he had to seek help from Morty.

Morty told him to wait a little while because he was in the middle of playing board game with his family. Ted said he'd used up all the fluid for his Portal Gun and now he didn't know where to get more. Beth told Morty to get Ted out of the gas. Jerry was being harassed by a bunch of tentacles emerging from the teleportation fluid. Ted then disposed of the souvenirs from those stupid old men into the Unnamed alien shredder and said he wouldn't be returning to that godforsaken place again. Morty quickly stopped Ted. He also saw a picture of Ted and Marjorie. They looked very happy. Ted forced Morty to get rid of it into the Unnamed alien shredder. He said it was now a poisonous substance. Ted said he had no intention of harming Morty, Morty a good kid and he deserves a better grandfather than that. After saying that, Ted pressed the red button.

Morty thought he was high, but no, it worked, but unfortunately, it worked too well.

In the post credit scene, Rick is on another vacation on a sea planet and is getting married to Unnamed alien bride. Here, Rick is Sallpock and quite well-liked. The priest asks if anyone objects to the wedding. Of course, Summer stands up to object, even though it's just a rhetorical question.

Sallpock said he didn't recognize Morty and Summer? He was planning to run away with the Unnamed alien bride when he was picked up by a spaceship.

title: Rickuiem Mort a Dream (plot)
text:
Hoping to gain some empathy from the cruelty of life, Morty is given a Sympathid given by Rick to become more understanding of everyone in life which soon spirals out of control. Meanwhile, Rick sends Summer and Jerry on an errand run which turns into an encounter with a serial killer.

Rick, having woken up in a good mood for once, decides to work in his underground distillery. He has a nice cup of coffee, a lump of breakfast, and puts little creatures into his ears which fart lo-fi music. He's also in possession of a Grimaldian potato, which he blends into a mixture. As he begins to work, Morty barges in despite a Do Not Disturb sign hanging on the door. Morty tries to get his attention, but accidentally destroys a fermentation chamber, causing a chain reaction that destroys everything. Rick gets extremely pissed at Morty, especially when he reveals he came in to ask to go get Pokémon cards with him. In a fit of anger, Rick reminds Morty that he was originally bait for Rick Prime and could have been abandoned at any time. This makes Morty upset, considering this was his greatest fear, and he runs back to his room. Rick realizes he went too far, but is more presently worried about his trashed distillery.

Rick tasks Summer and Jerry with getting the components needed to repair the distillery. He also needs a new Grimaldian potato as it was being used as starch for the alcohol, but there's only one left in the galaxy. Rick asks Morty for help, but Morty is still upset for being yelled at. Rick injects him with a Sympathid, a bug that generates empathy, which in practice alters Morty's perception of reality. Rick appears as caring, supportive grandfather due to his words being altered by the Sympathid. However, it does this by eating away at the empathy in Morty's brain to create stronger empathy. The two of them are able to win a dance competition to get the potato, and Rick removes the Sympathid to prevent lasting consequences. This leaves Morty at an empathy deficit, causing him to lash out.

Meanwhile, Summer and Jerry are having trouble getting drum containers due to them being sold out at multiple Home Depots. They see a guy loading a number of them into a truck, whom they also find out is a serial killer when he kidnaps a woman. Jerry wants to call the cops, but Summer doesn't want to risk having the drums be confiscated as evidence. She has Jerry pose as a fellow serial killer to lure the serial killer and buy the drums off of him, but he refuses due to not having change. He invites Jerry to his house, which Jerry accepts, wanting to rescue the woman.

Morty goes to get picked up by the school bus and gets harassed by a bully. Morty, still suffering come-down effects, decides to inject himself with the Sympathid again. The rest of his day at school is more peaceful, although Morty starts doing an excessive amount of empathetic and kind things, like comforting a crying teacher, stopping a fight, and working at a soup kitchen.

After driving over, Jerry gets locked inside the serial killer's house and drinks some tea with him. Summer breaks out of the trunk of the car and find the drums inside the basement. She also finds the woman trapped in a hole, who she rescues on the condition that she helps her move the drums outside. The serial killer reveals himself to be the Cat and Mouse killer, as he leaves a cat toy in his victim's pockets as a signature. Jerry attempts to improvise his own signature, but the Cat and Mouse killer gets creeped out from his bizarre explanation and calls the police.

Morty, still tripping from the Sympathid, apologizes to Rick about the earlier destruction of his distillery. Rick, oblivious of the Sympathid inside Morty, brings him to a mall and asks him to buy a thermometer. He does so, only for Rick to extract the Sympathid, which has grown into a massive brain-crab after devouring Morty's empathy centers. In reality, the two of them broke into a secure alien compound, and Morty just blew his arm off in a boobytrap while stealing the thermometer. Rick is mad, but is quickly humbled by Morty's new crueler personality. He insults Rick and shoots an alien in the gut and both knees before killing him, which Rick describes as ghoulish. The Sympathid attacks them again, but Rick prevents it from burrowing into Morty. It burrows into his mind instead, and Rick passes out.

Summer and the woman move the drums out to the car. They attempt to lift them to the roof of the car, but it drops onto the back windshield and turns on motion detecting lights on the front of the Cat and Mouse Killer's house, alerting him. The Killer ends up being more worried about the implication that Jerry was going to kill his daughter than the fact that his victim escaped. The cops arrive, and the Killer cries for help. Jerry ends up blabbing the plan in order to calm the Killer down, resulting in the Killer attempting to kill Jerry for causing him to call the police on himself.

Rick wakes up but is delirious and mostly incapacitated due to the Sympathid, so Morty is forced to break them out. He shoots several aliens dead and gets both of them to the Space Cruiser, where they escape. Summer calls them and forces Morty to go rescue Jerry. Due to his lack of empathy, Morty is able to sympathize and connect with an equally empathy-less Killer. Morty asks the Killer for a hug, something they both deeply desire. The Killer goes outside for a hug and is turned into a pile of flesh by the cops waiting outside.

Rick and Morty return home with the drums. Morty confesses that he feels disconnected from people without empathy. Rick shares this feeling and admits that he's a bad person for using the Sympathid to get what he wants from Morty. Morty accepts that as an apology and goes back to his room. Rick portals him a pack of Pokémon cards, but Morty still has no empathy centers and can't feel happy about it. Rick drinks some of the vodka he made from the potato, which purges and kills the Sympathid, ending the episode.

In the post credits scene, an extended version of Morty showing no empathy to a teacher at his school is shown where the teacher accuses him of being insensitive about her problems.

title: Salute Your Morts (plot)
text:
Seeing how Morty and Summer are abusing his devices, Rick drops them off at a Sleepaway camp where the kids make the rules, while Beth and Jerry have the house to themselves and end up tripping balls.

At Morty and Summer’s school, Principal Vagina has brought them along with Beth and Jerry into his office telling them that the two are expelled from the school due to abusing Rick's sci-fi equipment in the facility (along with using a muting machine to mute the adults’ voices). Hearing what happened, Rick (who just arrived from gardening) portals into the office and turns the principal into a carrot, traumatizing him enough to undo the kids' expulsion. Seeing that Morty and Summer are getting too spoiled because of him, Rick decides to send them an off world sleep away camp to help them out.

On the car ride over, Morty and Summer continuously pester Rick. Rick eventually gets fed up and extracts all of the robotic augmentations the two of them had via ripping them out with magnets and then healing them. He then ejects the two of them from a pod directly onto Camp Shergale, their brief new home. Although they assume it's a work camp ala Holes, the camp counselors reveal that they're actually allowed to do whatever they want, as the other kids took over the camp.

Meanwhile, Beth and Jerry realize they have the house to themselves. They raid Summer's room for drugs and find them hidden in a cabinet, although all of the drugs are alien and strange. They smoke a joint they found in a canister and get extremely high. However, they neglected to translate the label, called "High Forever".

The camp counselors are actually two other campers, as the real counselors were murdered by them years ago. Morty and Summer go on a tour, where everyone is doing fun but dangerous things. They learn that all of the stuff the campers have are Doordashed due to a bunch of them coming from rich families. The two of them decide to join the party lifestyle.

Beth and Jerry lament about being high forever. They decide to google a solution on Summer's computer and find that they need Darcan, which is like Narcan but from another solar system. They sneak into the garage, where Rick has been turning people into carrots and selling them, and get a space taxi from Zarz Dinnarz, a gelatinous bug kind of creature that absorbs them and alters its insides to resemble a limo. Jerry freaks out due to feeling like he's in a womb, but Beth comforts him. The two are motivated to stick their head out of the nonexistent sunroof for fun, which causes them to break out of Zarz Dinnarz. This leaves a hole in it and causes them to crash land into Planet Mart.

Morty and Summer party hard and get into a few fights, but they quickly get tired of the whole routine after a few days. They reach their breaking point when they witness a camper named Margo fart out a baby, which all the other campers attempt to make party. They try to leave, but are stopped by the campers and forced to feed beer to the fart baby before being allowed to do so.

Beth and Jerry navigate the mall and find the Darcan. They find it locked in a case, and get impatient when a store associate takes too way long to help them. They break it open with an axe and take the pills, but they start getting chased by a mall cop. They're able to hide in a storage area, but Beth finds out that Darcan only works for lifeforms with two hearts. Jerry calls Rick to bail them out. Rick portals there, but is also high forever.

Morty and Summer reach a town nearby and go to a bar to find a telephone. The townspeople are not happy to see them, assuming they're just like the other rabid campers, but allow them a call. Summer calls Rick and begs to leave, but Rick is incomprehensible and hangs up. In her call, Summer disclosed that the counselors were dead, meaning the campers were unsupervised. All of the townspeople pull out guns, planning to use the campers as ransom.

Beth, Jerry, and Rick understand that the kids are in danger and attempt to sober themselves up before rescuing them. Rick creates a portal leading to the other side of itself, and all three of them are unable to comprehend that this did nothing useful.

Meanwhile, the townspeople have kidnapped and tied all the campers up inside a shipping container, including Morty and Summer. Luckily, Beth, Jerry, and Rick all manage to portal inside and untie them. They're unable to portal back out because Rick left the portal gun back at Planet Mart. Summer realizes that they all smoked High Forever and are effectively useless, and rallies the other campers to save themselves. They decide that they need bow and arrows back at the camp, but need a distraction to get there. This distraction ends up being Rick, who they send at the guards. He cannot effectively fight, but all of his augmentations allows him to dodge bullets and kill them anyways.

The campers reach the shed and grab a bunch of weapons. They then go on a rampage, killing a ton of townspeople. They are about to kill the leader, the barkeeper, but she has taken Beth and Jerry hostage. She ends up getting distracted by Beth and Jerry saying something stupid, allowing the campers to get the upper hand, and she surrenders.

The family gets picked up by Space Beth in the Space Cruiser. Summer tells Beth and Jerry that their high will last for a few days as opposed to forever. Beth and Jerry get upset that Space Beth doesn't fuck them anymore, while Rick really wants to go Del Taco. Morty and Summer agree to get their shit straight to avoid embarrassing themselves like their parents (and Rick) did.

In the post credits scene, Jerry is showing his new ad idea for Cool Horse but freaks out when he hallucinates Rick watching him across the street eating carrots.

title: The CuRicksous Case of Bethjamin Button (plot)
text:
As Rick takes Jerry, Morty, and Summer to Earth World, Beth and Space Beth become kids again with the latter's machine and end up causing mayhem.

In an opening montage, Beth and Space Beth are seen waking up and performing their jobs both on Earth and space, but both find themselves dissatisfied with their lives. Upon returning to the Smith residence, Rick is planning a trip to Earth World, an alien theme park based on Planet Earth created by Dr. Dogballs. Rick invites the Beths to come with them but they both decline, opting to watch the house in their absence. After the group leaves, Beth laments that both of them are great at their jobs they do and yet are still unsatisfied with their life choices. When she thinks about reliving her childhood, Space Beth gets an idea to use an age manipulation chamber she uses to make transporting criminals easier to allow them to become kids again though the latter mentions they should be careful what they wish for.

Meanwhile, Rick, Jerry, Summer and Morty arrive at the park with Rick saying to them that Earth World is a creative mess and dangerous since the creators didn’t bother reading about Earth and its history. However Rick is dismayed and irate to find out Earth World has become family friendly with bobblehead like mascots of famous celebrities. Jerry and Summer run around to check the park, while Morty hooks up with an alien fangirl who has an obsession for humans.

Back on Earth, both Beths take turns using the age machine to relive their lives as kids but it turns out they're also extremely dangerous leading to killing animals and setting a makeshift treehouse with booby-traps. Eventually both of them end up as kids where they end up destroying the age machine to stay that way. Soon after the two decide to target Gene next door since he's easy to target. The two managed to get into his house where Gene offers to make hot chocolate for the duo. Soon after Gene is attacked by the Beths who soon turn on each other resulting in Gene's house burning up and de-gloves himself while attempting to call for help.

Upset with how Earth World is, Rick decides to sneak into the authorized personal area of the park by disguising himself, Summer and Jerry as the mascots using head enlarger collars after finding out that Dr. Dogballs is still alive. The three find him chained up in his office where he reveals that the Board of Directors of the Park put him under house arrest because of animal porn on his computer and without his guidance, the park has turned into the family friendly version it is today. He then takes them to the actual Earth World which is more run down and dangerous than the current one. In the middle of one of the rides, Rick gets an alert from Gene and portals back home to take care of things while leaving the remote for the collars in case they need to disguise themselves as mascots again.

After arriving home, Rick bribes the firefighters who rescued Gene from his house to keep the incident off tabs and restores his hand before heading back home to deal with the Beths. He soon runs afoul of all the booby traps in their tree house and the house before destroying the treehouse and restraining the Beths in containers with the intent of fixing the age machine to restore them back to normal. Back on Earth World, Dogballs takes Jerry and Summer to his hidden lab where the two discover that the mascots are actually Dogballs' living creations. It's then that he reveals that the real reason why the Board chained him up was that his endgame was to send the mascots to attack and kill the guests believing that to be the legacy of every theme park on Earth. He then activates a transmitter that causes all the mascots to become hostile while he himself is devoured by his own creations. Thinking fast, Summer uses the enlarging collars to disguise themselves while Morty who found the fangirl too clingy even for his standards escapes as well after she gets devoured. He's soon chased and attacked by a hydra like monster of the Culkin family but is soon rescued by Summer. They manage to steal a car to escape the park, but since Summer lost the remote to shrink their heads, they're forced to endure the coldness of space on the way back to Earth.

Meanwhile, Rick has finished fixing the age machine just as the Beths accuse him of abandoning them as Rick claims that's not true. They soon trick Rick into thinking one of them is suffocating and once he lets his guard down, they push him into the machine and turn it up to max power aging him by 3 centuries and attack him. However, instead of crying of sadness, Rick cries tears of joy revealing to them that his version of Beth died when they were her age He tells them that he's proud of them for pulling a fast one on him and they are his daughters regardless if they're clones or not. Hearing this along with seeing a vision of their father, the two realize they're assaulting the wrong person and tearfully hug him ending their rampage.

Sometime later, both Beth and Space Beth, now returned to their normal ages are seen performing their jobs again, but this time have a newfound appreciation for their lives. They also fix up Gene's house as a way to make up for all the trouble they caused while Rick rebuilds their tree house without any booby traps and enjoy the sunset. At that time, Morty, Summer, and Jerry crash land in the backyard, the latter two of the three suffering from burns and sores from being exposed to the space vacuum due to their enlarged heads. Rick gives them an 'I told you so' about Earth World being terrible as the Beths look on in confusion.

In the post-credit scene, Rick's cell phone is seen overflowing with voicemails coming from Gene to 911 (which is actually rerouted to Rick) about all the disasters he's seen from the Smith family, with the last one has him saying that the number should never have answering machines.
